clue.text: Envoys coming from announcement of relay team's composition

indicators.note: an announcement is something spoken out, so we want the sound of the phrase rather than its spelling

parts.note: a relay team is made up of four runners, as in the 4 x 100 metres

explanation.surface: Messengers arriving with news of who has been picked for the relay squad.
explanation.definitionFit: Forerunners are those sent ahead to herald what follows, much as envoys or harbingers go before.

clue.text: Busy minx, loud rather than hard

indicators.note: one thing put in place of another, so one letter is swapped for a different one

parts.note: a minx is a cheeky or brazen girl
f is forte, the musical direction for loud
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A cheeky girl kept occupied, and noisy rather than tough.
explanation.walkthrough: Put F in place of the H of HUSSY to get FUSSY.
explanation.definitionFit: A design that is too busy is cluttered and over-elaborate, which is what fussy means of decoration.

clue.text: What may be read after dictator loses his head and goes berserk

indicators.note: going berserk is running wild, so the remaining letters are thrown into a new order
losing the head means the opening letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A tyrant is overthrown and runs amok, prompting the authorities to restore order.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the riot act is the idiom for a stern reprimand; the Riot Act was a British law read aloud to disperse crowds.
explanation.definitionFit: The Riot Act was a statute formally read out to unruly crowds, hence the idiom of reading someone the riot act.

clue.text: Invigorated having been given a new tablet!

parts.words: having been given a new tablet!
parts.note: surface reading: a patient revived by fresh medicine in pill form

parts.words: having been given a new tablet!
parts.note: setter's reading: a Kindle is an e-reader tablet

explanation.surface: Someone perked up after being handed a fresh pill.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation mark flags the pun: the Amazon Kindle is a reading tablet, and the word splits as RE + KINDLED.
explanation.definitionFit: To rekindle is to relight or revive, so something rekindled has been given fresh energy.

clue.text: Conservative hurried back to argue

indicators.note: going back means the word is read from its last letter to its first

parts.note: hurried means ran
to row is to quarrel

explanation.surface: A Tory politician rushed back for a political fight.
explanation.definitionFit: Narrow in the sense of narrow-minded describes a conservative, unadventurous outlook.

clue.text: Fraternal American entertained by brothel keeper

indicators.note: being entertained by is being hosted inside, so the answer sits within the following words

parts.note: the letters run across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: A member of an American brotherhood being shown a good time by a madam.
explanation.walkthrough: The Elks are a US fraternal society, the Benevolent and Protective Order of Elks, so a member is an Elk.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the Elks, an American fraternal lodge, is known as an Elk.

clue.text: Head of school's short test for band

indicators.note: cut short means the final letter is lopped off
the head of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letter of the word
a trial is a test

explanation.surface: A headteacher's quick audition to pick players for a school band.
explanation.definitionFit: A stria is a thin stripe or ridge, so a narrow band of colour or texture.

clue.text: Georgia's natural resource

parts.note: GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia
the possessive ending taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a fact about Georgia, but GA plus the S of the possessive spells the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Natural gas is an extracted fuel, a classic example of a natural resource.

clue.text: General transported a farm worker

indicators.note: transported means carried away or moved about, so the letters are shifted into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An army commander shipped off a labourer from the fields.
explanation.definitionFit: A gleaner gathers leftover grain after the harvest, a traditional kind of farm labourer.

clue.text: Drunk sailor's had to provoke, as it were

parts.note: a sot is a drunkard
OS is an ordinary seaman

indicators.note: as it were suggests something only seemingly so, so we want a word that merely sounds right

parts.note: to pique is to provoke or irritate

explanation.surface: A drunken seaman had set out to pick a fight, in a manner of speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: The final words do double duty: they define the answer and also signal that the provoking word is wanted by sound only.
explanation.definitionFit: So to speak and as it were are interchangeable phrases flagging a figurative way of putting things.

clue.text: Clerk's to trek with Bob touring suburbia

indicators.note: touring means wandering about, so the letters travel into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An office clerk sets off on a hike with his friend Bob around the suburbs.
explanation.walkthrough: The stockbroker belt is the British name for the affluent commuter suburbs around London, especially in Surrey.
explanation.definitionFit: The stockbroker belt is a wealthy commuter zone outside a city, a particular kind of suburbia.

clue.text: Long story about leader of Egypt

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: a yarn is a tale

indicators.note: the leader of a word is the letter at its front

parts.note: the opening letter of the country's name

explanation.surface: A lengthy tale about the first pharaoh of Egypt.
explanation.walkthrough: Long looks like an adjective describing the story, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To long for something is to yearn for it, both verbs of strong wanting.

clue.text: Lead-free waste and rubbish containing Iodine and pigments

indicators.note: containing means holding inside, so one piece goes within another
free of its lead means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: soil is waste matter, as in night soil
pants is British slang for rubbish, as in that film was pants
I is the chemical symbol for iodine

explanation.surface: An environmental notice about unleaded waste, junk, iodine and dyes.
explanation.walkthrough: Lead-free reads like a note about petrol or paint, but it removes the first letter. Pants meaning nonsense is everyday British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Oil paints are pigments ground in oil, so they are colouring materials an artist applies.

clue.text: Taste speed

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to try with the tongue

explanation.walkthrough: Both words look like nouns or verbs of different worlds; at a fair lick is a British idiom for at a good speed.
explanation.definitionFit: A lick is a taste with the tongue, and also an informal word for a brisk pace.

clue.text: Small part of Stuart in film?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the surname of the mouse hero of the film Stuart ...

explanation.walkthrough: Part of Stuart suggests taking letters from that name, but it means a piece of the film title, the mouse's surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Little is a plain synonym for small, and also the second word of the film title Stuart Little.

clue.text: "Translators maybe translating tussling", I interposed

indicators.note: interposed means placed between, so a single letter is slotted inside the other letters
translating means converting into another form, so these letters are turned into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A quoted remark about interpreters wrestling over a text, with the speaker butting in.
explanation.definitionFit: Linguists are language specialists, and translators are one kind, hence the hedging maybe.

clue.text: After next month a union may be so unscathed

definitions.text: After next month a union may be so
definitions.meaning: first meaning: the union with Scotland might end, leaving the UK free of Scots
second meaning: escaping without penalty or harm

explanation.surface: A prediction that a marriage or alliance could come through next month unharmed.
explanation.walkthrough: The puzzle appeared in August 2014, a month before Scotland voted on leaving the United Kingdom, so the Union might have ended up literally Scot-free.
explanation.definitionFit: To get off scot-free is to escape without punishment or injury, so wholly unscathed.

clue.text: Thence reference is included in an article on memory

indicators.note: being included in something means sitting inside it

parts.note: the definite article
ROM is read-only memory in computing
ref is the usual abbreviation for reference

explanation.surface: From there, a citation appears in a piece written about remembering.
explanation.walkthrough: The reference is included in the whole phrase an article on memory, so it goes between the two parts, not inside the article alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Therefrom is a formal word meaning from that place or thing, exactly the sense of thence.

clue.text: Start again after Catholic quits belief system

indicators.note: something that quits leaves, so a letter departs from the word

parts.note: a credo is a set of beliefs
C is the abbreviation for Catholic

explanation.surface: Starting over in life once a Catholic abandons the faith.
explanation.definitionFit: To redo something is to do it again from the start.

clue.text: Important person stops to welcome old insignificant people

indicators.note: welcoming someone means taking them in, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: a nob is a toff or person of rank
an engine that stops dies
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A grandee halts to greet some elderly people of no account.
explanation.definitionFit: Nobodies are people of no importance, the plural noun fitting insignificant people.

clue.text: Religious books about saint without a protective cover

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first piece wraps the second

parts.note: Bibles are scriptures
S is the abbreviation for saint

explanation.surface: Holy books concerning a saint, lacking a dust jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: Protective cover suggests a book jacket, but it is a bib, so the answer is BIB-LESS.
explanation.definitionFit: A bib protects clothes while eating, so to be bibless is to lack that protective covering.

clue.text: Graduate engineer has cards to trim

parts.note: BE is Bachelor of Engineering
a deck is a pack of cards

explanation.surface: A newly qualified engineer gets a hand of cards to cut down.
explanation.definitionFit: To trim in the sense of decorate, as with a dress or a tree, is to bedeck or adorn.

clue.text: Etch English duck in a colour — quite the reverse

indicators.note: in places one thing inside another
this flips the preceding instruction, so the outer and inner parts swap roles

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, shaped like O
taken as written
a tint is a shade of colour

explanation.surface: Engraving a plump English duck in some hue, or vice versa.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, E and O would go inside A TINT; the closing words turn that round, so A TINT sits between E and O.
explanation.definitionFit: Acid etches metal by gradually corroding it, which is what eat into means.

clue.text: Camera accessory seen in college compartment

parts.note: uni is short for university
a pod is a detachable compartment, as on a spacecraft

explanation.surface: A photographer's gadget spotted in a university locker.
explanation.definitionFit: A unipod is a single-legged stand used to steady a camera, a common photography accessory.

clue.text: Article in Le Monde describing British nuclear boffin returning without being observed

indicators.note: to describe a shape is to draw round it, so one piece encloses another

parts.note: une is the French indefinite article
B is the abbreviation for British

indicators.note: returning means coming back, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for nuclear
a wonk is an expert obsessed with a specialist field

explanation.surface: A French newspaper reports on a British atomic scientist sneaking back home.
explanation.walkthrough: Le Monde is a French paper, so the article wanted is French. Boffin is British slang for a scientist or expert.
explanation.definitionFit: Unbeknown means without someone knowing, so done unseen or unnoticed by them.

clue.text: Car model's right to incorporate a bit of plastic material

indicators.note: to incorporate is to take inside, so a letter goes within the other pieces

parts.note: the Ka is a Ford model
OK means all right

indicators.note: a bit of a word here is just its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A car is fine to have some plastic built into it.
explanation.definitionFit: Kapok is a fluffy fibre from a tropical tree, used as stuffing, so a kind of material.

clue.text: Additional passage court dismissed

indicators.note: something dismissed is sent away, so those letters leave the word

parts.note: an extract is a passage from a text
CT is the abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: A further section of a trial where the court threw out the case.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra means more than usual, a direct synonym for additional.

clue.text: Nest by a lake

parts.note: taken as written
Erie is one of the North American Great Lakes

explanation.surface: A bird's nest built beside a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: An aerie, or eyrie, is the high nest of an eagle or other bird of prey.

clue.text: Parenting repels distressed business associate

indicators.note: distressed means upset or knocked about, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Raising children puts off an upset colleague.
explanation.walkthrough: Parenting and sleep make a tempting pair, but the phrase is a British business term.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleeping partner invests in a firm without taking part in running it, so a silent business associate.

clue.text: Religious messenger is half-cut _

definitions.note: a noun here: a religious is a member of a religious order

indicators.note: cutting something in half removes half of it, so half the letters go

parts.note: a nuncio is a papal envoy

explanation.surface: A church envoy has had a few drinks too many.
explanation.walkthrough: Half-cut is British slang for drunk, but here it trims half the letters off the end.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun, a religious is a monk or nun under vows, so a nun fits.

clue.text: Very special plea

parts.note: so means very, as in so good
S is the abbreviation for special

explanation.walkthrough: Very special reads as an adjective phrase on plea, but both words supply letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An SOS is a distress signal, hence any urgent appeal or plea for help.

clue.text: Commissioner imprisoned in royal vault for eternity

parts.note: a king is royal

indicators.note: imprisoned in means locked inside, so one piece is held within another

parts.note: a dome is a vaulted roof
Com is the abbreviation for commissioner

explanation.surface: A senior official locked in a palace crypt for all time.
explanation.walkthrough: Vault suggests a crypt, but it is the arched roof.
explanation.definitionFit: Until kingdom come is an idiom for forever, so kingdom come stands for the afterlife or eternity.
